purpose: Provide a minimal Privacy-owned, operation-bound purpose and terminal withdrawal record for P8-17 current-authority proof; it is not participant consent or a production email-change requirement.

implementation_revision.semantics: WELL-18 introduces a proof-only Privacy state, immutable transition history, a database guard against initial withdrawal, and a transaction-locked current-authority read at Identity's protected mutation boundary. The map is refreshed against the committed source checkpoint and is not governing authority.

collaborating_domains.interface: Identity.apply_primary_email_change/1 calls NewYou.Privacy.require_current_p817_proof_purpose_locked/2 inside the owning Account transaction when the development/test proof gate is enabled.
collaborating_domains.ownership: Identity alone owns Account, Session, Token and primary-email mutation. It reads current Privacy authority and never stores a copied permission or performs Privacy writes.

ash.caller_boundary: Privacy-owned Ash Resource and owner functions; allowed-to-withdraw is terminal, and the current row is locked for Identity's authoritative re-read.
Append-only Privacy-owned evidence of grant and withdrawal version; it never authorizes an Identity mutation.
Identity owns the source mutation and obtains current Privacy authority inside its same PostgreSQL transaction before applying the canonical email change.

arguments: Identity Account UUID and primary-email operation UUID.
returns: A withdrawn operation cannot be regranted.
side_effects: Development/test only: create one operation-bound allowed authority row and version-1 grant event through Privacy Ash actions in one transaction.
caller_constraints: This synthetic purpose is a proof fixture, not participant consent, registration acceptance or production policy.

arguments: Identity Account UUID and operation UUID for the existing proof-only authority.
returns: {:ok, :withdrawn | :already_withdrawn}, {:error, :missing} when no current row exists, or a closed Privacy error.
side_effects: Locks and transitions the Privacy row to withdrawn, increments its version and appends the matching immutable event atomically.
caller_constraints: Development/test only. Missing records do not create negative state; no restoration transition exists.

arguments: Identity Account UUID and operation UUID while the source transaction includes PurposeAuthority.
returns: :ok only for a current allowed row held FOR UPDATE; missing or withdrawn denies and unavailable reads fail closed.
side_effects: Locks the durable Privacy current-state row through the same Repo transaction as the source mutation; no Identity copy or cache is written.
caller_constraints: Caller must already be inside the Identity authoritative transaction; a request-start or UI read is insufficient.

returns: Existing Identity apply result; proof-gated negative or unavailable Privacy authority maps to the existing unavailable result.
side_effects: After existing Identity Account, Session, Token, proof, delay and review checks, re-reads and locks current Privacy authority immediately before target mutation.
caller_constraints: The P8-17 check exists only in development/test and only when the dedicated proof flag is enabled; ordinary primary-email change does not require new consent.

request_flow.summary: Registration persists Terms and Privacy version acceptance under Identity; a successful registration leaves the separate operation-bound Privacy proof purpose missing.
A development/test fixture asks the Privacy owner to grant the synthetic purpose for an existing Identity operation; a separate Privacy owner call may withdraw it.
Identity's source transaction locks Account, Token and Session authority, then obtains a current FOR UPDATE read from Privacy immediately before its protected mutation.

guards: Only the Privacy-owned development/test proof fixture can create this exact synthetic purpose and origin for one subject and source operation.
PostgreSQL rejects initial state other than allowed at version 1, even when a matching withdrawn event is supplied.
The unique subject/purpose/source-operation key prevents a second competing current row.
side_effects: Create current authority at version 1 and append the matching granted event in one Ash transaction.

guards: Privacy locks the current authority row; the only accepted state change is allowed to withdrawn with exactly one version increment.
PostgreSQL lifecycle guards reject regrant, delete, truncate, provenance edits and version skips.
side_effects: Update current Privacy state and append the matching withdrawn event atomically.

security_invariants.summary: Privacy owns the purpose/withdrawal row and event history. Identity reads the current result but does not store a competing grant or write Privacy truth.
The only stored purpose and origin are the P8-17 synthetic protected-mutation proof and its fixture origin; both owner writes and Identity enforcement are development/test gated.
Registration Terms/Privacy acceptance is distinct from purpose-specific permission; registration alone leaves the proof purpose missing.
Missing, withdrawn, negative or unavailable current Privacy authority fails closed. The affected Identity operation does not accept browser, Session, operator, cache or workflow permission snapshots.

concurrency.summary: Identity locks Account, sorted related Token rows and Session rows before locking the Privacy current-purpose row. Privacy withdrawal locks only the purpose row, so the selected path has no reverse Account/Token/Session lock dependency.

Both source mutation and withdrawal contend on the same PostgreSQL Privacy row. If withdrawal commits first, Identity reads withdrawn and denies; if Identity locks and commits first, withdrawal waits and records a later withdrawal.

idempotency_retry.summary: Grant and withdrawal retries return stable existing states; grant after terminal withdrawal is denied and cannot recreate a positive row.

A denied Identity apply retry re-reads current Privacy state; a fresh BEAM process after withdrawal remains denied, while a source mutation that serialized first is already applied and is not undone by later withdrawal.

failure_recovery.summary: A missing row denies, and an unavailable Privacy owner read maps to the existing Identity unavailable result without source mutation or downstream apply consequences.
Purpose state is read from PostgreSQL by a fresh process after restart; no process-local flag, cached projection, browser state, Session or Audit record can restore withdrawn permission.

cases: Privacy creates allowed state and versioned grant history.
Withdrawal is terminal, appends matching immutable history, and cannot be regranted or deleted.
Withdrawing a missing operation returns missing and does not create negative authority.
A current locked read rejects withdrawn authority and a fresh process reads durable withdrawal.
PostgreSQL rejects both an authority grant and withdrawal that lack their version-matched event at transaction commit.
PostgreSQL rejects an initial withdrawn authority even when matching history is supplied.
Concurrent first-time grants serialize through the unique operation key and resolve against one committed allowed row and one event.
tests.proves: The Privacy owner actions and PostgreSQL constraints preserve operation-bound current truth and transition history.
tests.limits: Owner operations are synthetic development/test proof fixtures; this does not implement participant consent UX or legal-purpose policy.

cases: Initial RED: missing current purpose did not deny before implementation.
Withdrawal commits before source's locked current read, then mutation and stale retry deny without apply consequences.
Source transaction locks current allowed state first; PostgreSQL reports real withdrawal contention and source commits before later withdrawal.
Fresh BEAM retry after committed withdrawal denies.
tests.proves: The Identity source transaction and Privacy withdrawal serialize on the same durable PostgreSQL authority row in both commit orders.
tests.limits: The selected primary-email mutation is only gated by the synthetic purpose in development/test when the dedicated proof flag is enabled; no production consent requirement is introduced.

safe_extensions.summary: A future production purpose requires its own approved purpose semantics and Privacy-owned interface before it can use this demonstration; P8-17 does not create one.
Privacy is registered as an Ash domain but is explicitly outside Identity reconciliation; an additional unreviewed domain still blocks reconciliation apply.

reuse.summary: Reuse the existing NewYou.Repo PostgreSQL Ash transaction and Identity P8-16 Account/Token/Session lock sequence; do not add a service, cache, Repo or write API.
The certified Phase-7B Privacy dossier disposition remains NOT_REQUIRED; this implementation records only its source-linked code capability map.

prohibited_shortcuts.summary: Do not infer purpose permission from registration acceptance or copy a positive Privacy result into Account, Session, operator view, workflow or another Domain.
Do not use an unlocked request-start read, cache, process state, Audit evidence or derived projection as authority at Identity's mutation boundary.
Do not expand the proof into a consent centre, production primary-email consent rule, legal-basis engine, deletion/export orchestration or a new Privacy dossier.

proof_limitations: The demonstration purpose and its grant/withdraw actions compile only for development/test; the Identity apply guard is likewise test/development-only and flag-controlled.
PostgreSQL order is proven using separate local TEST connections and observed pg_blocking_pids contention. The proof does not model cross-region database failures.
Unavailable owner-read behavior is exercised with the established deterministic test seam; it does not simulate every physical database outage mode.
The proof does not establish a production legal consent requirement and does not alter the certified Privacy JIT dossier disposition.
